'''''Erkenntnis''''' is a journal of [[philosophy]] that publishes papers in [[analytic philosophy]]. Its name is the German word "[[wiktionary:Erkenntnis|Erkenntnis]]", meaning "knowledge, recognition, insight". The journal was also linked to organisation of conferences, such as the [[Second Conference on the Epistemology of the Exact Sciences]], of which it published the papers and accounts of the discussions.

==First series (1930–1940)==
When [[Hans Reichenbach]] and [[Rudolf Carnap]] took charge of ''Annalen der Philosophie und philosophischen Kritik''<ref name="annalen">[https://link.springer.com/journal/12375/volumes-and-issues Annalen der Philosophie und philosophischen Kritik]</ref> in 1930, they renamed it ''Erkenntnis'',<ref name="erkenntnis">[https://link.springer.com/journal/10670/volumes-and-issues Erkenntnis]</ref> under which name it was published from 1930 to 1938. The journal was published by the ''Gesellschaft für Empirische Philosophie'', or the [[Berlin Circle]] and the [[Verein Ernst Mach]], [[Vienna]]. In the first issue Reichenbach wrote that the editors hoped to gain a better understanding of the nature of all human knowledge through consideration of the procedures and results of a variety of scientific disciplines, while also hoping that philosophy need not remain a series of "systems" but could reach the state of objective knowledge.<ref name=Hempel>Hempel, C. G. (1975). [https://www.ualberta.ca/~francisp/NewPhil448/HempelOnErkenntnis.pdf The Old and the New 'Erkenntnis']. Erkenntnis 9(1), 1-4</ref> The final issue of the first series, Volume 8, No. 1, was published in 1939 and retitled ''The Journal of Unified Science (Erkenntnis)'' (1939–1940) and included as associate editors [[Philipp Frank]], [[Jørgen Jørgensen (philosopher)|Jørgen Jørgensen]] ([[:da:Jørgen Jørgensen_filosof]]), [[Charles W. Morris]], [[Otto Neurath]], and [[Louis Rougier]]. The advent of [[World War II]] led to the cessation of publication.<ref name=Hempel></ref>

==Second series (1975–present)==
In 1975 the journal was "refounded" by [[Wilhelm K. Essler]], [[Carl G. Hempel]], and [[Wolfgang Stegmüller]], and it has been published continuously since.<ref name=Hempel></ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.springer.com/cda/content/document/cda_downloaddocument/10670_erkehem.pdf?SGWID=0-0-45-127906-p35759970 |title=''idem'', download |access-date=2017-08-28 |archive-date=2020-11-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201114092000/https://www.springer.com/cda/content/document/cda_downloaddocument/10670_erkehem.pdf?SGWID=0-0-45-127906-p35759970 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The editor-in-chief is [[Hannes Leitgeb]] ([[LMU Munich]]), and the supervisory board comprises [[Michael Friedman (philosopher)|Michael Friedman]] ([[Stanford University]]), Hans Rott ([[University of Regensburg]]), and [[Wolfgang Spohn]] ([[Konstanz University]]).<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.springer.com/philosophy/journal/10670?detailsPage=editorialBoard |title=Editorial Board |access-date=2017-08-28 |archive-date=2017-09-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170920095954/https://www.springer.com/philosophy/journal/10670?detailsPage=editorialBoard |url-status=dead }}</ref>
